newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after recovery fizzles.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after recovery fizzles.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker after a brief mid-session recovery fizzled ahead of an expected rise in LME stocks Friday, traders said.
Despite some inevitable profit-taking early in the session, most of Wednesday's large 4.75 cent gain was still intact.

"The reason why it's going up is that the trade was convinced that the market was too high, and the squeeze would attract stocks, which it did, and then it would just die after February 14 but it does not look like it," a broker said.
Traders expected LME stocks to rise modestly by a few thousand tonnes Friday.

Arbitrage related hikes in U.S. LME stocks were due to dwindle by now. Nearby LME cash is still at modest premium over COMEX, but by the Feb 19 LME date the market switches to a COMEX premium over LME.
"But if the tightness on LME continues past the February date, then the arbitrage will start up all over again," the broker added.
March COMEX copper settled 0.15 cent weaker at 108.60 cents per pound, traded 109.25 to 106.75 cents. Spot February went out 0.50 cent lower at 109.50 cents.
